membership.note: candidates_for_lane(lane_id) returns the same 2 rows (join) for every lane; union of store member ids = all 10 candidates ids 1..10

maturity_audit: computed from evidence strength, not constant. Member level (build.py maturity_for_members): low if verified_refs<=0; high if verified_refs>0 AND (has_measured_result OR has_external_verdict); else medium. Lane level: high if every member high; medium if at least half the members are non-low; else low. Live: all 10 candidates carry verified_refs=2 of 2 and no measured result / no CONFIRMS|EXTENDS verdict, so every member is medium and every lane is medium. The fixture in tests/test_lanes_build.py:173-197 proves the branches really differ (201=high, 202=medium, 205=low), and guard-b's red run showed 211=high vs 212=medium in the same lane. Caveat: the live 10-candidate store exercises only the 'verified-only' branch, so 'medium' x5 is a correct computed value that would be indistinguishable from a constant on this store alone.
audience_audit: computed from the members' kinds, not hardcoded. audience_for_kind maps a kind through an ordered 19-marker table (measured|benchmark|eval|performance -> evaluators; unreproduced|unverified|unfalsifiable|claim|contradict -> verifiers; superseded|decision|regression -> maintainers; novel|primitive|invariant|enforcement|boundary|implementation -> practitioners; no marker -> 'technical readers'); audience_for_members takes the highest AUDIENCE_PRIORITY and forces evaluators when any member has a measured result. Live: all 10 real candidates are novel_primitive (x5) or invariant_or_enforcement (x5) -> practitioners for every lane, so only 1 of the 5 audience values is exercised live (fixture proves evaluators/practitioners variation).
